newsitem.title: UK: Thatcher says will fight for Conservative victory.
newsitem.headline: Thatcher says will fight for Conservative victory.

text.p: Former British prime minister Margaret Thatcher on Monday endorsed her successor John Major and said she would be fighting with "all her strength" for a Conservative Party victory in the May 1 election.
"Stay with us and with John Major until we cross the finishing line," Thatcher told reporters outside her London office.

Thatcher accused Tony Blair's main opposition Labour Party of concealing its old-style socialist intentions. "The phrase New Labour is cunningly designed to conceal a lot of old socialism," she told journalists.
Thatcher also dismissed suggestions that voters would vote out the Conservatives because they wanted a change after 18 years.
"People say "time for a change'. That's absurd. If you have a good builder, dare I say it a good grocer, or a good government you should stick with it," she said.
Thatcher also attacked Labour's pledge to stick to the government's current spending targets, saying Labour would automatically spend more. "I do not expect to see a prime minister Blair," she said.
